assertions.name: borromean_canonical_is_not_a_tetrahedral_decomposition
assertions.source: Vol(L6a4)/Vol(tetrahedron) is not an integer, so the canonical decomposition of the corpus's principal manifold is not a triangulation into regular ideal tetrahedra

assertions.name: octahedron_is_not_an_integer_multiple_of_tetrahedron
assertions.source: an ideal octahedron is not an integer number of regular ideal tetrahedra, reinforcing the previous check

assertions.name: derived_layered_fig8_has_two_tetrahedra
assertions.source: the braid-word-derived layered triangulation of S^3\4_1 has two tetrahedra (one per letter of the LR word RL)

assertions.name: derived_layered_volume_matches_canonical
assertions.source: the derived layered triangulation carries the full hyperbolic volume to the 45 significant digits its producer serializes (residual 4.94e-45 = that truncation), so it is a decomposition of the same complete structure

assertions.name: pachner_distance_candidate_vanishes_on_fig8
assertions.source: layered and canonical cell counts agree, so the candidate observable is 0 on the one knot the framework can derive both for

data.scope: A volume identity is consistent with a cell structure, it does not prove one; the octahedral and two-tetrahedron decompositions are classical and are cited. What is measured here is that the corpus registry agrees with them, that the Borromean volume admits no tetrahedral re-reading, and that the Pachner-distance candidate is 0 on 4_1. It is NOT a claim that a Pachner distance is uninformative on a manifold where the two decompositions differ; no such manifold is currently derivable in this corpus.
